claim: Action potential patterns of sensory cortex neurons encode a variety of stimulus features.
source_text: Action Potential (APs) patterns of sensory cortex neurons encode a variety of stimulus features

claim: An STDP protocol consisting of pairing a postsynaptic AP with visually driven presynaptic inputs modifies a neuron's AP-response in a bidirectional way that depends on the relative AP-timing during pairing.
source_text: in vivo a spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) protocol—consisting of pairing a postsynaptic AP with visually driven presynaptic inputs—modifies a neurons' AP-response in a bidirectional way that depends on the relative AP-timing during pairing

claim: APs repeatedly preceding presynaptic activation reduce AP responses to visual stimulation.
source_text: APs repeatedly preceding presynaptic activation reduce AP responses to visual stimulation

claim: The reported lack of dependence of the peak changes on the millisecond timescale is not consistent with previous in vitro STDP studies.
source_text: What is not consistent with previous in vitro STDP studies, where synaptic efficacy changes were derived from post-synaptic potentials, is our reported lack of dependence of the peak changes on the milisecond timescale
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparison of the current findings to prior in vitro work.

claim: From in vitro studies it would be expected that a pre-before post pairing with a delay during pairing of around 40 ms would produce almost no change and a pre-before post with a delay of around 2 ms would produce the most change.
source_text: From in vitro studies it would be expected that a pre- before post pairing with a delay during pairing of around 40 ms would produce almost no change and a pre- before post with a delay of around 2 ms would produce the most change
evidence_reasoning: This is a characterization of expectations from prior in vitro work, cited from Bi and Poo (1998).

claim: The reported initial peak changes were not at t = 0 but were seen for a diverse range of timings within a time range of ∼100 ms.
source_text: Our reported initial peak changes were not at t = 0 but were seen for a diverse range of timings within a time range of ∼100 ms
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The discrepancy with previous studies is due to the complexity of in vivo responses to visual stimulation which are made up of an avalanche of both inhibitory and excitatory synaptic events.
source_text: We suggest that this discrepancy with previous studies (also see Fregnac et al., 2010) is due to the complexity of in vivo responses to visual stimulation which are made up of an avalanche of both inhibitory and excitatory synaptic events
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation of why the results differ from in vitro studies, citing Hirsch et al. (1998) and Okun and Lampl (2008).

claim: It is an oversimplification to capture complex in vivo responses by measuring only the peak of the initial response.
source_text: It is therefore an oversimplification to capture such complex responses by measuring only the peak of the initial response
evidence_reasoning: This is a methodological insight about the limitations of peak-only analysis.

claim: Measuring the evoked voltage across the entire time course of the response and aligning the voltage changes around the timing of pairing APs revealed a very robust timing dependence.
source_text: Here we measured the evoked voltage across the entire time course of the response and aligned the voltage changes around the timing of pairing APs. With this approach we were able to show a very robust timing dependence, not just of an isolated synaptic input, but of the integrated inputs made up of multiple synaptic events
evidence_reasoning: This is a methodological approach and finding from the study shown in Figure 5A-C.

claim: Peak response changes occurred at about 30–50 ms before and after the pairing spike.
source_text: We found peak response changes at about 30–50 ms before and after the pairing spike
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from the experimental data.

claim: The discrepancy between in vivo and in vitro peak timing is due to the very precise pre-synaptic timing during the pairing protocol from one trial to the next used in in vitro STDP studies which is contrary to the variable L4 and L2/3 visual response latencies found in vivo.
source_text: Our model suggests that this discrepancy is due to the very precise pre-synaptic timing during the pairing protocol from one trial to the next used in in vitro STDP studies which is contrary to the variable L4 and L2/3 visual response latencies found in vivo
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion from the modeling work, citing Fagiolini et al. (1994) and Niell and Stryker (2008) for the variable latencies.

claim: In four cases increases in AP firing were significant at the single-neuron level (p<0.05) for positive timing inductions.
source_text: In four cases increases in AP firing were significant at the single-neuron level (p<0.05), despite the modest numbers of stimulus presentation trials and low firing rates
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical result from the experimental data.

claim: Changes in spiking after negative timing were statistically significant at the single-neuron level (p<0.05) in four cases, all of which showed a decrease in spiking.
source_text: These changes were statistically significant at the single-neuron level (p<0.05) in four cases, all of which showed a decrease in spiking

claim: Increases in AP firing at the paired position for positive timing inductions remained significant even after removing the two neurons exhibiting the greatest increases (p=0.036, n = 13).
source_text: Finally, we note that increases in AP firing at the paired position for positive timing inductions remained significant even after removing the two neurons exhibiting the greatest increases (p=0.036, n = 13)

claim: Of the 15 neurons tested with positive timing, 11 showed an increase in the average number of APs evoked by stimulus presentation, 1 showed a decrease, and 3 never discharged a stimulus-evoked AP.
